raw_segments.text: These two women may be much upon a par, with respect to reason and humanity, and changing situations might have acted just the same selfish part.
But had they been differently educated, the case would also have been very different.
The wife would not have had that sensibility, of which self is the center, and reason might have taught her not to expect,
and not even to be flattered by the affection of her husband, if it led him to violate prior duties.
She would wish not to love him, merely because he loved her, but on account of his virtues,
and the sister might have been able to struggle for herself, instead of eating the bitter bread of dependence.
